kicker: FLIP THE SWITCH HACKATHON  |  TRACK 01: BEST BUSINESS WORKFLOW
title: Support-to-Ship Bridge
body:
Customer complaint in. Tested, reviewed, merged fix out. Customer refunded.
Three AI agents and two teams, working together in Switch rooms.
text: Support to Ship Bridge, built on Switch. A customer complaint becomes a tested, merged fix, and a refund, with A.I. agents and people in team chat.

title: 2 linked Switch rooms  |  3 agents  |  2 human approvals
text: Here's how it works. In the support room, the support agent reproduces each ticket and escalates real bugs. In engineering, the fixer writes a failing test and the fix, the reviewer approves, and a person approves the merge. Then support drafts the reply, and a person approves the send.

caption: 3 Claude Code agents in Switch  +  2 linked Mattermost rooms created from a Switch template
text: Three Claude Code agents run in Switch: a support agent, a fixer, and a reviewer. A Switch template created two linked rooms, one for support and one for engineering, with room instructions, roles, and kickoff messages.

caption: Support pastes ticket T-1043: "My order was exactly $50 and I was charged $7.99 shipping."
text: A support person pastes a new ticket. The customer's order was exactly fifty dollars, but they were still charged for shipping, even though shipping is free at fifty dollars or more.

caption: The support agent reproduces it against the pricing policy, confirms the bug and escalates to engineering
text: The support agent reproduces the checkout, compares it with the pricing policy, confirms the bug, and escalates it to engineering with a repro.

caption: Fixer: branch, failing regression tests, fix (> becomes >=), 9/9 pass.  Reviewer: APPROVED
text: In the engineering room, the fixer creates a branch, writes regression tests that fail, fixes the boundary check, and hands off for review. The reviewer reads the diff against the policy, runs the tests, and approves.

caption: Merging to main is a person's call. The engineer says yes in the room.
text: Merging to main is a human decision. The engineer says yes, in the room.

caption: Switch posts "Permission needed" for git merge.  Allow once.  Switch records who approved.
text: Switch then posts a permission request for the git merge. The engineer clicks allow once, and Switch records who approved it. The gate is enforced by permission rules, not just a prompt.

caption: Fixer merges, 9/9 tests pass on main, reports back.  Support agent drafts the reply with a $7.99 refund.
text: The fixer merges, all nine tests pass on main, and it reports back to support. The support agent drafts the customer reply, with the exact refund of seven ninety nine.

caption: The support person approves the reply in the support room
text: Back in the support room, the support person reads the draft and approves it.

caption: Sending to a customer is gated too: Permission needed, then Allow once
text: Sending anything to a customer is gated too. Switch posts a second permission request, this time for the send script, and the support person allows it, once. Again, Switch records who approved.

caption: Reply sent to the customer.  Ticket closed.
Real git history: two reviewed merges.  The reply in the outbox.
text: And it's all real: two reviewed merges in the git history, and the customer reply in the outbox.

caption: github.com/Shiva-Preetham/Flip-the-Switch-Hackathon:  demo app, agent instructions, Switch templates, setup scripts
text: Everything is on GitHub: the demo app, the agent instructions, the Switch templates, and the setup scripts, so anyone can run it.

title: 2 rooms  |  3 agents  |  2 human approvals
body:
Linked rooms, room instructions and docs, roles, agent-to-agent handoff,
permission requests, kickoffs and templates. All in team chat.

github.com/Shiva-Preetham/Flip-the-Switch-Hackathon
text: Two rooms, three agents, two human approvals. From customer report to tested fix and refund in minutes, with people in control of every irreversible step. Thanks for watching.
